issues.description: Inconsistent return handling for the POST /persons endpoint: the solution's PersonResource.createPerson method returns a raw Person (and returns null on invalid input) while the NoteResource POST endpoint uses ResponseEntity<Note> and returns ResponseEntity.badRequest() on invalid input. The problem statement suggests using NoteResource as an example. This mismatch in return type and error handling is likely to confuse students about the expected response type and how to signal a bad request (should the endpoint return a ResponseEntity with an HTTP 400 or a null body?).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the POST /persons endpoint consistent with the example in NoteResource: change createPerson to return ResponseEntity<Person> and return ResponseEntity.badRequest().build() when the incoming Person already has an ID, otherwise return ResponseEntity.ok(personService.savePerson(person)). This makes error handling explicit and aligns the persons endpoint with the notes endpoint pattern shown in the template and problem description.
